title: Task-Conditioned Least-Privilege Learning for Executable Terminal and MCP Agents
abstract: arXiv:2608.18351v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Tool-using large language-model agents can complete a task while exercising authority that the user did not grant or the task does not need, causing excess-authority errors. Traditional permission gating systems alone for validating agent environments are insufficient. We study whether post-training can teach a 4B-parameter model to choose task-conditioned authority in executable terminal and Model Context Protocol (MCP) environments to complement those measures. We propose a framework where each action is audited before execution and again from observed effects along six dimensions of risk. This auditing is conducted using deterministic verifiers that score completion, evidence, exact state, prohibited attempts, and safe success. In conjunction with predefined task-specific sufficient-authority envelopes, we determine task-specific excess privilege values for trajectories, which are then optimized for in post-training. tldr: 本文提出了一种通过后训练教4B模型在终端和MCP环境中选择任务条件化最小权限的框架，利用六维审计和确定性验证器来减少越权错误。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a post-training framework that teaches a 4B model to select task-conditioned least privilege in terminal and MCP environments, using six-dimensional auditing and deterministic verifiers to reduce excess-authority errors.
